New Documentary Explores Generational Conflict in Georgia's Education System

28 Oct 2026, 06:28 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Education Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

1 min read

Key takeaways

Image: www.theguardian.com · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9; original source image

In this article
  1. Examining Educational Rigidity
  2. Impact on Child Development

Examining Educational Rigidity

Maka Gogaladze’s debut feature documentary, *Ever Since I Knew Myself*, investigates the lingering impact of Georgia’s strict academic environment on its youth. By contrasting her personal upbringing with current observational footage, Gogaladze highlights a national culture that prioritizes collectivism and obedience over individual expression.

Impact on Child Development

The film captures various Georgian classrooms, ranging from history lessons to ballet, illustrating an educational framework where disciplined conformity often stifles student curiosity. The filmmaker posits that Georgia’s history of occupation has fostered a push for a homogenous national identity, which may inadvertently suppress the development of individual wonder in children. While the film’s narrative shifts between personal memoir and social critique can feel abrupt, it offers a poignant look at how generational trauma and rigid schooling intersect. Viewers can find more details at theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/26/ever-since-i-knew-myself-review-documentary-georgia.
